facts.raw_span: A man in his 50s presented with a 12-year history of itchy eruptions over the whole body
Multiple nodules appeared on the upper back 1 year previously and gradually increased in number and size
extensive, dry scaly patches on the trunk, arms, and legs
Several 0.5- to 1-cm, dome-shaped, red papules and nodules were found on the upper back
Mildly enlarged lymph nodes were observed on the cervical, axillary, and inguinal regions
Routine blood tests, biochemistry analyses, and peripheral blood flow cytometry tests were within normal limits
No atypical cells were found in the peripheral blood
DNA analysis from paraffin sections showed clonal amplification product for the γ-chain of the T-cell receptor
Atrophy of the epidermis with focal orthokeratosis
Extensive, dense infiltrate of lymphocytes in the entire dermis
Small to medium-sized, atypical lymphocytes with focal areas of epidermotropism
Positive for CD2, CD3, CD4, and CD45RO

concepts.why: The patient's presentation of itchy eruptions, dry scaly patches, and dome-shaped nodules, along with the histopathological findings of atypical lymphocytes and epidermotropism, are consistent with Mycosis fungoides, a type of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma.

aliases: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma with leukemic involvement
concepts.why: The patient's presentation of itchy eruptions, dry scaly patches, and atypical lymphocytes, along with the histopathological findings of epidermotropism, are consistent with Sézary syndrome, a type of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma with leukemic involvement.
The patient's presentation of itchy eruptions and dry scaly patches is consistent with atopic dermatitis, a chronic inflammatory skin disease.
The patient's presentation of dry scaly patches and dome-shaped papules is consistent with psoriasis, a chronic inflammatory skin disease.
The patient's presentation of enlarged lymph nodes and atypical lymphocytes is consistent with cutaneous lymphoid hyperplasia, a benign condition that can mimic lymphoma.
The patient's presentation of dome-shaped papules and atypical lymphocytes is consistent with lymphomatoid papulosis, a rare skin condition that can mimic lymphoma.
The patient's presentation of dry scaly patches and dome-shaped papules is consistent with granuloma annulare, a benign skin condition.
The patient's presentation of itchy eruptions and dry scaly patches is consistent with pityriasis rubra pilaris, a rare skin condition.

rationales.F01: Itchy eruptions are common in many skin conditions, but the long history and whole-body involvement are more suggestive of mycosis fungoides or atopic dermatitis.
rationales.F02: Nodules on the upper back are more typical of mycosis fungoides or lymphomatoid papulosis.
rationales.F08: Clonal amplification of the T-cell receptor gamma chain is highly suggestive of a T-cell lymphoma, such as mycosis fungoides or Sézary syndrome.
rationales.F11: Atypical lymphocytes with epidermotropism are characteristic of mycosis fungoides.
rationales.F12: Positive staining for CD2, CD3, CD4, and CD45RO is consistent with a T-cell lymphoma, such as mycosis fungoides or Sézary syndrome.

frontier_selector.rationale: Mycosis fungoides is the most likely diagnosis due to the presence of extensive, dry scaly patches, multiple nodules on the upper back, and histopathological findings of atypical lymphocytes with epidermotropism, which are all characteristic of this condition.
